accepts.because: a turn to screen before it reaches the agent. The caller MUST promote the identity to context.channel, or every surface shares one bucket and is rate-limited as one. context.user_id is the SECOND identity dimension: the sender rules address it by name (field 'user_id', two rows in the shipped seed), and a caller that never promotes it leaves that whole rule class matching the empty string -- an allow row on user_id then rejects every turn, and a deny row on it never fires

emits.because: the turn survived every rule; this is the only lane into the agent behind it
the turn was refused. hop.reject_reason and hop.rule_id say what happened; what to do about it is the parent's decision

description.purpose: Scope marker of the firewall: bundles the deterministic screen and its rule store behind one entry lane and two exit routes. Every inbound turn of a channel passes it before anything agentic is reached, and leaves either unchanged on 'pass' or refused on 'reject' with the rule that fired named on the hop.
description.use_when: One per ingress channel, between the surface and the agent's intake. Instantiate it in the same mutation that wires the ingress lane and BOTH exits; the hive is an island until an edge crosses into it.
description.not_in_scope: No model anywhere -- whether a turn is admissible is decided by comparisons and a clock. No outbound speech: the firewall never answers the sender. No rewriting: a passed turn is byte-identical to the one that arrived.
